## Outcome

PR #286 finally merged after a long review cycle. I then spent most of the week contributing to Toby Hocking’s PR #253, where fixed-aspect plots were preserving the data ratio but not making good use of wide or tall viewports.

## Context

The panel-margin branch began before GSoC. During Week 10, I completed its review changes and merge. PR #253 is owned by Toby Hocking; my contribution covered implementation, tests, documentation, and later simplification work.

## What I Did

- Merged [PR #286](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/286) on July 29.
- Added scale-to-fit behavior and wide/tall viewport tests to [PR #253](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/253).
- Preserved the data aspect ratio while allowing the panel to use the largest available area.
- Updated the long-running facet-strip branch after the main-branch text behavior changed.

## Learnings

I initially focused on preserving the relationship between x and y. The remaining problem was choosing the largest panel that fit the viewport without stretching that relationship.

## Challenges / Notes

Browser coordinates differed by tiny floating-point amounts. I had to ignore harmless SVG noise without making the test too loose to catch the real aspect-ratio bug.

## Next Week Targets

Rerun the open renderer branches after the recent upstream changes and record what still needed review.

<iframe src="week10-panel-margin-demo/index.html" title="Three Animint facet plots comparing zero, one, and two lines of panel margin" loading="lazy"></iframe>
:::

The three plots use identical Iris data. Only `panel.margin` changes, so the increasing space between facet panels is directly visible.

<details class="demo-code">
<summary>View the essential R code</summary>

```r
margin_plot <- function(lines) {
  ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length, colour = Species)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~Species, nrow = 1) +
    theme(panel.margin = grid::unit(lines, "lines"))
}

animint(
  zero = margin_plot(0),
  one = margin_plot(1),
  two = margin_plot(2)
)
```

</details>
